blogs.title: The October inflection point for vibe game development
blogs.description: I've written before about how November 2025 was an inflection point for coding agents - the point where Opus 4.5 and GPT-5.1 crossed a tipping point that meant their respective coding agents became reliable daily drivers for software engineers. I think we've reached a new inflection point in October 2026, and this time it's for vibe coding computer games.

blogs.name: Simon Willison
blogs.title: Quoting Terk Terkowitz
blogs.description:
If your work does not benefit from current AI tooling, that is a finding, not a failing. Document why, share it with your community of peers, bring it to your manager, and work to find solutions. An engineer who can explain where AI does not yet help their work is demonstrating the judgement we are asking for.

—

blogs.name: Julia Evans
blogs.title: Testing Vue components in the browser
blogs.description:
Hello! One of my long term projects on here is figuring out how to write frontend Javascript without using Node or any other server JS runtime.

One issue I run into a lot in my frontend JS projects is that I don’t know how to write tests for them. I’ve tried to use Playwright in the past, but it felt slow and unwieldy to be starting these new browser processes all the time, and it involved some Node code to orchestrate the tests.
